description: AirGuard Chicago is an interactive web application that uses NASA satellite data and ground-based air quality measurements to analyze air pollution in Chicago. By combining NASA TEMPO satellite observations with EPA monitoring data, our project helps users explore pollution levels, identify trends, and understand how air quality changes over time.
summary:
For our project, we built TrendScope, an interactive website that helps people understand how Earth's environment is changing over time.

The idea came from a simple question: How can we tell if a place is actually getting warmer, or if we're just seeing normal weather changes?

With TrendScope, you can explore a 3D globe, click on any location, and look at over 40 years of NASA environmental data. The website shows temperature, precipitation, humidity, and other measurements through graphs. It also uses statistical tests to show how fast things are changing and whether those changes are significant. We also added visualizations for wind, air pollution, humidity, and solar radiation.

Our project addresses the NASA challenge by making it easier to find and understand environmental trends in different parts of the world. We wanted to create something that anyone could use, even without a background in data science.

We hope TrendScope helps more people explore real environmental data and better understand what's happening to our planet.
details:
TrendScope is an interactive website that lets people explore how the environment has changed over the past 40 years.

Users can rotate a 3D globe, select a location, and see graphs showing changes in temperature and other environmental conditions. We also added statistical tests to help show how fast things are changing and whether the trends are significant.

We built the website using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and MapLibre. We used NASA POWER for historical data, NASA GIBS for Earth imagery, and Open-Meteo and CAMS for current environmental estimates.

Our main goal was to make complicated environmental data easier to understand. Instead of looking through large datasets, anyone can explore real data on an interactive globe and learn how different places are changing over time.
